resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register places the tower in Cedars of Lebanon State Park (a state park, administered by TDEC). Forest Lookouts files it under Cedars of Lebanon State Forest, which is a different designation. The story reports both and does not choose.
The Register gives 782 ft (238 m); Tennessee Landforms gives 794 ft for Hurricane. The story reports both.

Only Forest Lookouts gives a construction year (1936). Tennessee Encyclopedia says a lookout tower and nursery were also built on the site, in its account of the park's development, but does not name or date the tower, so it cannot be tied to this tower with certainty.

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build year rests on one line from Forest Lookouts; it is the only construction date found. Height 32.9 m is the brief figure and matches 108 ft. The Register and Forest Lookouts disagree on whether the site is a state park or state forest. Tennessee Landforms lists the tower under the name Hurricane (code WLT001). The tnstateparks.com highlights page returned HTTP 403 and livingnewdeal.org returned 403, so neither was read. A search for the Hurricane tower on the park's own site may settle the climbing question.
